comparison: Both address the main IGF-1 findings (C2-C5, C22-C24, C81, C93) but reach different conclusions. OpenEval rates as UNSUPPORTED due to failure to survive Bonferroni correction, while peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN. Peer reviewers are more critical, stating 'none of the genetic variants can be deemed as causal' and that conclusions are 'unreliable,' whereas OpenEval acknowledges the limitation but focuses on the nominal significance not being sufficient evidence.

OpenEval R2 addresses IGF-1 sensitivity analyses (C25, C39-C41) rated as UNCERTAIN due to inconsistent results across methods. Peer R1 encompasses these claims within their broader critique of IGF-1 findings, emphasizing the multiple testing problem affects all 657 SNPs investigated. Both express uncertainty but peer review focuses more on the fundamental statistical validity issue.

Both address null findings for testosterone and SHBG (C6, C26-C31) and agree these are SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes the statistical appropriateness of reporting null results. Peer reviewers also accept these findings, noting 'This is another trial finding no association of sex hormones to COVID-19,' but requested better contextualization of negative results.

Both address sex-stratified analyses (C32-C38) showing null results. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, acknowledging appropriate interpretation despite wide confidence intervals for estradiol. Peer R2 includes these claims in their acceptance of null sex hormone findings, with both noting the weak instrument limitation for estradiol (C63).

Both address contextualization with observational literature (C42-C45). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, finding appropriate discussion of prior work. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, emphasizing 'lack of any real-world validation cohort' and 'lack of any transcriptomic data,' suggesting literature citations alone are insufficient without experimental validation.

Both address biological mechanisms for IGF-1 (C46-C55). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, noting well-cited established knowledge presented appropriately as speculative. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, questioning whether 'IGF-1-related SNPs influence IGF-1 levels in the context of viral infection' and whether they constitute eQTLs, emphasizing lack of direct experimental evidence.

Both address IGF-1 and estrogen interactions (C56-C63). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, praising appropriate acknowledgment of null estradiol findings with biological context. Peer R2 includes C63 in their acceptance of null sex hormone findings, with both noting the weak instrument limitation for estradiol.

Both address testosterone literature and contextualization (C64-C73) and agree these are SUPPORTED. OpenEval praises 'thorough and balanced discussion' of contradictory literature. Peer reviewers accept these background claims and requested more extensive contextualization of negative results, which this discussion provides.

Both address study design and data sources (C13-C21, C83-C85). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, emphasizing large sample sizes and standard methodology. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, identifying 'important details' missing (winner's curse bias), questioning r2 cutoff choices, and noting inadequate handling of confounders like dexamethasone treatment and BMI.

Both address study limitations (C74-C80) and agree these are SUPPORTED. OpenEval praises 'honest and comprehensive discussion of limitations.' Peer reviewers explicitly raised these limitations and accepted the authors' acknowledgment, though they suggested limitations undermine the strength of conclusions more than authors indicated.

OpenEval R11 addresses methodological details (C86-C110) rated as SUPPORTED, noting comprehensive description and standard MR procedures. Peer R4 overlaps on some claims (C90-C91, C103-C107) but rates as UNCERTAIN, questioning specific choices like r2 cutoff and noting various unhandled biases, suggesting execution concerns despite standard approaches.

OpenEval R12 addresses statistical methods (C94-C100) rated as SUPPORTED, praising appropriate methods, proper citations, and adherence to STROBE guidelines. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses these statistical methodology claims, though peer R4's methodological concerns focus more on study design choices than statistical analysis procedures.
